about: Zenkai Rules Z1 intent examples for scripts/htc_post_run.sh (rows 458/461/463, the HTC post-run runbook). Run by tests/intent/test_htc_post_run_intent.py against a fake run dir -- never a real gauntlet run, never darktable.
subject: scripts/htc_post_run.sh

examples.why: the ordinary post-run case: the run finished and the runner already exited cleanly, so the script prints the five-step batch for a human to run -- step 1 (fix round 3, review R3b) calls tests/mutation_check.py directly, not `make gate` (whose own wrapper falls back to a bare python3 with no pytest from a worktree)
a run still in progress must never hand off into merge/push -- this is the guard the whole script exists for
progress.json can say done while the runner process itself has not exited yet (e.g. mid-report); the pid check is the second, independent oracle for that

input.progress_status: blocked: darktable pids [69648] were not launched by the gauntlet; quit them first

examples.why: row 493/495: the loop can stamp progress.json 'blocked: <reason>' instead of ever reaching done -- the run still counts as OVER once preconditions 2 and 3 (runner pid gone, no live process for the stamp) hold, same two independent oracles as the done case, so the post-run batch is not stuck refusing a run that has genuinely ended
